jobs.occupation: Master Thesis in Aerodynamics in the  Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department (d/f/m) (Elektroniker/in - Luftfahrttechnische Systeme)
jobs.description: About usAirbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.Job descriptionIn order to support the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department, Airbus Operations is looking for aMaster student (d/f/m) in the field of Aerodynamics in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics departmentYou are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of a job title? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department as a master student (d/f/m)!- Location: Hamburg- Start: 01.06.2025- Duration: 6 monthsYour opportunity- Are you passionate about aircraft physics?- Are you keen to master the way we compute external loads acting on the vehicle due to maneuvers, flight in turbulence, landing impact, ground-handling?- Do you like to work in an empowered manner?- Do you enjoy connecting people and collaborating with many different interfaces?- This job will give you the opportunity to work internationally with several internal flight physics departments and with teams located in Europe and India.About usWe are a team of 16 multicultural and passionate engineers who perform the gust calculations for overall aircraft design for all aircraft types. Our team is involved from a very early design stage until certification and also in-service support. We are responsible for running build model activities such as finite element modeling, creating mass and aerodynamics models. We perform gust loads calculation, including failure cases, and deliver to internal interfaces. On top, we are deeply involved in research and technology aspects with new aircraft configuration assessments, model based system engineering, automation and machine learning.IntroductionThe current industry approaches of modeling unsteady aerodynamic flow for the prediction of gust loads typically assume linear flow conditions. Linearity greatly reduces the computational time required to evaluate all the flight points and gust conditions required by the certification specifications (CS-25). At the same time, disregarding non-linearities such as boundary layer separation arising from the high angles of attack induced by strong gusts can lead to an over-estimation of loads and thus to an increased structural weight of the aircraft.Your locationYou will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.Your benefits- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.- Work with modern/diversified technologies.- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.Your tasks and responsibilitiesDuring this six months Master thesis you will develop and evaluate an unsteady aerodynamic model that includes the effect of flow separation in a piecewise linear approach. The model will be built using linearized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of a complete flexible aircraft and adapted using aerodynamic data obtained in the non-linear flow region at high angles of attack. You will evaluate the model by comparison against higher-fidelity models, such as obtained from non-linear time domain simulation, with respect to gust loads.You will contribute to:- Optimize the design of Airbus commercial aircraft in the frame of new wing technologies- the development of new approaches to model unsteady aerodynamics considering non-linearities for gust loads and flutter computation- Actively support us as a new member of our team on our journeyDesired skills and qualifications- You are a fulltime enrolled master student (d/f/m) within Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent- You have good knowledge in aerodynamics, CFD and potential flows- Ideally you already have first experience in CFD using TAU or CODA- You have knowledge in coding using Python and/or Matlab- You bring basic knowledge in overall aircraft design and basic competencies in flight loads calculation and flight mechanics- You are passionate to understand physical aspects and to use your engineering judgement- If you are familiar with tools like MSC.NASTRAN or ALTAIR HyperWorks, this is beneficial- You are a highly motivated, proactive and open-minded person with a great sense of initiative- You are keen to deepen your technical knowledge while enjoying to work in a multicultural team- Your English is at negotiating levelPlease upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.Not a 100% match? jobs.occupation: Scientific software engineer (f/m/d) in SWI Science Operations (Astrophysiker/in, Astronom/in)
jobs.description: The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Göttingen is one of the world's leading research institutions in the fields of solar physics and planetary research, with approximately 300 employees. These include hardware simulator as well as expected science data modeling. This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, data science, and instrument operations, offering a unique opportunity to shape how science data is processed, calibrated, and interpreted in real mission contexts.You will play a key role in advancing the SWI software infrastructure from data pipelines to mission planning tools by embedding physically accurate models that enable precise interpretation of observations and support autonomous, science-driven operations.Your Tasks- Maintain, enhance, and build upon existing SWI science operations tools and ground segment data pipeline (mostly Python)- Integrate these models into science operations workflows, enabling predictive simulations for observation planning and calibration- Contribute to the development of automated science operations systems, including scheduling, anomaly detection, and real-time data assessment- Collaborate closely with the SWI science team, mission operations, and software engineers to ensure seamless integration of models into the ground segmentYour Qualification- A PhD, MSc (or soon to be completed PhD) in Physics, Astronomy, Planetary Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, including science software engineering- A solid Python programming skills, C language, Docker and Gitlab familiarity- Proactive mindset, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to work in a collaborative, interdisciplinary environment- Good command of spoken and written EnglishOur Offer- Comprehensive onboarding, professional development and further training opportunities- Diverse and varied tasks in an international work environment- Remuneration according to TVöDBund, based on qualifications and experience, annual bonus and additional pension scheme (VBL)- 30 days of vacation plus 4 additional days off- Full-time and part-time employment; flexible working time and possibility of mobile work- Cooperation with local bilingual Montessori child care center- Good public transport connection- Corporate health managementWe offer• A dynamic, international research environment at the forefront of planetary science and space instrumentation• The opportunity to contribute to a flagship ESA mission with long-term scientific impact• Support for professional development, including training, conference participation, and collaboration with leading institutions• A supportive team with strong expertise in both software engineering and planetary scienceAdditional Information- The position is rated in acccordance to public service act (TVöD-Bund) as EG 13- Position can be filled from January 2027 (a sooner start can be considered)- Initial contract is until end of 2027, extension may be possible depending on project funding- Application deadline is Nov 30, 2026Ergänzende Informationen:Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach VereinbarungAnforderungen an den Bewerber: Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Virtualisierungssoftware Docker, Programmiersprache C, Versionsverwaltungsprogramm GitLabExpertenkenntnisse: Programmiersprache Python
